ADVANCE HEALTH CARE DIRECTIVE
OF HELENA MARGARET OSGOOD

I, Helena Margaret Osgood, of 4417 Beacon Ridge Road, Charlotte, North Carolina 28209, being of sound mind, make this Advance Health Care Directive to state my wishes about my health care and to appoint an agent to make health care decisions for me if I become unable to make them myself. I revoke any prior advance directive, living will, or health care power of attorney I have signed.

PART 1. APPOINTMENT OF HEALTH CARE AGENT

1.1 Agent. I appoint as my health care agent:

Raymond Osgood, my brother, of 812 Sedgefield Lane, Charlotte, North Carolina 28209, telephone (704) 555-0148.

1.2 Alternate Agent. If Raymond Osgood is unwilling, unable, or unavailable to act, I appoint as my alternate agent:

Dr. Priya Anand, my friend, of 233 Queens Road West, Charlotte, North Carolina 28204, telephone (704) 555-0192.

1.3 When the Appointment Takes Effect. My agent's authority becomes effective when my attending physician determines in writing that I lack the capacity to make or communicate my own health care decisions, and it ends when I regain that capacity.

1.4 Authority of My Agent. My agent may make any health care decision I could make for myself, including the authority to:

(a) consent to, refuse, or withdraw consent to any care, treatment, service, or procedure to maintain, diagnose, or treat a physical or mental condition;

(b) select and discharge health care providers and institutions;

(c) approve or refuse the administration of medication, surgery, and artificially administered nutrition and hydration, subject to the instructions in Part 2;

(d) receive and consent to the disclosure of my medical records, and my agent is my personal representative for purposes of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its implementing regulations at 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164; and

(e) authorize my admission to or discharge from a hospital, hospice, nursing home, or other medical facility.

1.5 My Agent Must Follow My Wishes. My agent shall make decisions consistent with the instructions in Part 2 and with what my agent knows of my wishes and values. If my wishes are unknown, my agent shall act in my best interest.

PART 2. INSTRUCTIONS ABOUT END-OF-LIFE CARE

2.1 If My Condition Is Terminal and Incurable. If my attending physician and one other physician determine that I have an incurable and irreversible condition that will result in my death within a relatively short time, I direct that life-prolonging measures be withheld or withdrawn, and that I be permitted to die naturally, with only the care necessary to keep me comfortable and to relieve pain.

2.2 If I Am Permanently Unconscious. If two physicians determine that I am unconscious and, to a high degree of medical certainty, will never regain consciousness, I direct that life-prolonging measures be withheld or withdrawn.

2.3 Artificially Administered Nutrition and Hydration. I direct that artificially administered nutrition and hydration be withheld or withdrawn in the circumstances described in Sections 2.1 and 2.2. I understand that this may hasten my death.

2.4 Relief from Pain. I direct that I be given medication to relieve pain and to keep me comfortable, even if that medication may hasten my death, and that comfort care never be withheld.

2.5 Pregnancy. If I am pregnant at the time this directive would otherwise apply, my agent and my physicians shall follow North Carolina law governing the effect of pregnancy on an advance directive.

PART 3. OTHER PROVISIONS

3.1 Organ Donation. I wish to donate any needed organs, tissues, or eyes for transplantation, therapy, or research, and I have registered as a donor with Donate Life North Carolina.

3.2 Primary Physician. I designate Dr. Marcus Whitfield, Providence Family Medicine, 6015 Park South Drive, Charlotte, North Carolina 28210, as my primary physician.

3.3 Effect of Copy. A copy of this directive has the same effect as the original.

3.4 Nomination of Guardian. If a guardian of my person must be appointed, I nominate my agent named in Part 1.

3.5 Revocation. I may revoke this directive at any time and in any manner that communicates my intent to revoke, whether or not I have the capacity to make health care decisions.

3.6 Governing Law. This directive is made under the laws of the State of North Carolina, including Chapter 32A and Article 23 of Chapter 90 of the North Carolina General Statutes.

SIGNATURE

I sign this Advance Health Care Directive on June 12, 2026, and I am at least 18 years old, of sound mind, and acting freely and voluntarily.

______________________________
Helena Margaret Osgood

WITNESSES

Each of us declares that the person who signed this directive did so in our presence, that the person appears to be of sound mind and under no duress, fraud, or undue influence, that neither of us is related to the person by blood or marriage, that neither of us would inherit from the person under any will or by operation of law, that neither of us is the person's attending physician or an employee of that physician, and that neither of us has a claim against the person's estate.

NOTARY ACKNOWLEDGMENT
